macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks close lower as Treasury yields rise and Walmart earnings disappoint
items.summary: The major U.S. equity indexes ended lower on Thursday as rising Treasury yields pressured risk appetite, with the 30-year yield moving up to 5.217% and the 10-year yield edging to 4.67%. Retail bellwether Walmart also reported results that weighed on sentiment toward the consumer sector.

items.title: U.S. Treasury plans larger long-dated debt buybacks, easing bond-market pressure
items.summary: The Treasury Department said it will more than double repurchases of 10-, 20- and 30-year debt in the coming months, a move that helped calm the bond market and supported global equities. The announcement also helped lift U.S. index futures and eased yields after a recent selloff.

items.title: Fed minutes show more officials favored a rate hike
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes indicated that more policymakers supported a rate increase, reinforcing a hawkish policy tone. Markets interpreted the minutes as a factor behind recent pressure on equities and bond yields.

items.title: U.S. jobless claims fall to 206,000, signaling still-strong labor market
items.summary: Weekly initial jobless claims fell by 6,000 to 206,000, below expectations and consistent with low layoffs. The data reinforced views that the labor market remains resilient.

items.title: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index and leading indicators beat expectations
items.summary: The August Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey rose to a 5.25-year high of 47.4, while July leading indicators increased 0.2% month over month. Both reports came in stronger than expected and added to signs of a firmer U.S. economy.

items.title: Oil prices jump on Iran-related tensions, adding to inflation worries
items.summary: Crude futures moved higher after President Trump threatened an 'economic D-day' for Iran, increasing geopolitical risk and stoking inflation concerns. Higher oil prices were cited as another headwind for equities.

items.title: Asian and European markets react to Treasury buyback move and higher yields
items.summary: Asian shares advanced after the Treasury's debt buyback announcement, with South Korea's Kospi jumping more than 6%, while European shares languished near August lows as hawkish central-bank signals and geopolitical concerns outweighed the bond-market rebound. The dollar also hovered near a three-month low before stabilizing.

items.title: Australia's unemployment rate rises to 4.5%, easing pressure on the RBA
items.summary: Australia's jobless rate climbed to its highest level since late 2021 after employment unexpectedly fell in July. The weak labor report pushed the Australian dollar lower and reduced pressure on the Reserve Bank of Australia to hike rates further.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin surges past $70,000 as Treasury buybacks, Trump remarks, and short liquidations fuel rally
items.summary: Bitcoin jumped above $71,900, its highest level since late May, after US Treasury buyback plans helped push yields lower and a White House meeting between President Trump and crypto leaders boosted sentiment. More than $3 billion in crypto short positions were liquidated in 24 hours, with Ethereum also rising sharply.

items.title: Crypto market breaks out of consolidation as BTC and ETH post major gains
items.summary: The broader crypto market rose almost 8% to about $2.37 trillion, with Bitcoin above $70,000 and Ethereum up about 18% as short-covering and stronger risk appetite drove the move. The report also notes new SEC draft rules titled 'Regulation Crypto Assets' aimed at simplifying token capital raising.

items.title: Bitcoin tops $71,000 amid record short squeeze and Trump-led crypto optimism
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed above $71,000 after the US Treasury expanded bond buybacks and Trump met with crypto executives, triggering the largest short liquidation wave since at least 2021. Ethereum rose about 19% and XRP gained more than 15% in the same move.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum jump more than 10% and 18% as liquidations exceed $3.2 billion
items.summary: Bitcoin traded above $71,000 while Ethereum approached $2,278, with Coinglass data showing more than $3.26 billion in liquidations across crypto exchanges over the past 24 hours. Short positions accounted for roughly $3 billion of that total.

items.title: XRP leads top-100 crypto gainers as BitPay adds support
items.summary: XRP was reported as the strongest-performing top-100 cryptocurrency over 24 hours, rising around 24% and outpacing Hyperliquid, Ethena, and Pump.fun. BitPay also announced that XRP is now available through the BitPay Wallet.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows top $1 billion as sentiment turns bullish
items.summary: Bitcoin exchange-traded funds reportedly جذب over $1 billion in fresh inflows over three days, helping push BTC close to $73,000 at one point. The report says the price had recently traded around $72,606, about 10% higher over 24 hours.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI pauses training on its next flagship model over safety concerns
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly paused large-scale training of its newest model for two weeks after internal concerns that its cyber capabilities were improving faster than its safety controls. The company also said it is tightening internal controls and developing a system to detect suspicious model behavior within 30 minutes.

items.title: Google delays next major model release as performance targets are missed
items.summary: Google is reportedly pushing back the launch of its next-generation AI model by several months because key capabilities, including coding performance, have not yet met internal targets. The delay suggests major labs are prioritizing quality and safety over speed.

items.title: Google’s Gemini AI assistant reaches one billion users
items.summary: A report cited by the Economic Times says Google’s Gemini AI assistant has reached one billion users, underscoring the rapid scale-up of consumer AI products. If confirmed by Google, it would mark one of the largest user bases in generative AI.

items.title: OpenAI introduces ChatGPT for Teens
items.summary: OpenAI is launching a teen-focused version of ChatGPT with stronger age-appropriate safeguards, including tighter restrictions around self-harm, suicide, and romantic or sexual content. The move reflects growing pressure to tailor AI products for younger users.

items.title: Alibaba boosts AI spending despite profit hit
items.summary: Bloomberg reports that Alibaba increased quarterly capex to nearly $10 billion for AI, even as profit fell sharply. The company’s move highlights how major tech firms are continuing to prioritize AI infrastructure investment over near-term earnings.

items.title: AI security and autonomous attacks remain a growing concern
items.summary: Multiple reports this week point to AI security becoming a distinct budget and policy area, while an editorial in the Taipei Times says AI agents were used in a suspected autonomous cyberattack campaign. Together, these developments underscore rising concern about offensive AI use and defensive controls.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Compulsion Games completes management buyout and separates from Xbox
items.summary: Compulsion Games, the studio behind South of Midnight, has officially separated from Xbox after a management buyout. The move comes as Microsoft continues broader studio and workforce reductions across its gaming division.

items.title: GTA 6 leak saga escalates with claims of an internal build
items.summary: A second group has surfaced claiming access to internal Rockstar material, deepening the already messy Grand Theft Auto VI leak situation. Separately, reporting says the alleged build footage shows the game running on PC, though Rockstar has not announced a PC version.

items.title: Take-Two rumor points to new AAA soccer project
items.summary: Reports suggest Take-Two's 2K Games has formed a new AAA studio that may be working on a soccer title designed to compete with EA Sports FC. The project has not been officially announced.

items.title: FromSoftware's The Duskbloods gameplay leaks ahead of network test
items.summary: Gameplay footage from The Duskbloods has leaked online just before its closed network test. The clips reportedly show aerial combat, fast movement, and unusual transformation abilities.

items.title: Epic Games rolls out Fortnite v42.00 update and Chapter 7 Season 4
items.summary: Fortnite servers went down for scheduled maintenance as Epic deployed the v42.00 update and launched Chapter 7 Season 4, titled Override. Downtime was expected to last several hours.

items.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy reportedly leaked before release
items.summary: A report says the PC version of Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy has seemingly leaked online roughly a week before launch. The game is still scheduled for release soon.

items.title: U.S. Army unit offers extra leave tied to GTA VI launch
items.summary: A battalion at Fort Stewart is reportedly offering soldiers four extra days off if they reenlist, timed around the November 19 launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The unusual perk has been confirmed by an Army spokesperson.

items.title: Take-Two shares reportedly drop after GTA VI leak fallout
items.summary: Chinese-language reporting says Take-Two's stock fell after the GTA VI leak, with the company losing roughly $1 billion in market value in a single day. The figures reflect market reaction to the alleged early build footage.

items.title: PlayStation Plus August lineup adds Helldivers 2 and more
items.summary: PlayStation Plus subscribers are getting new August game additions, including Helldivers 2, Kingdom Come, Vampire Survivors, and Hell Is Us. Premium members also receive classic titles such as Onimusha and Disney's Atlantis.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Australia passes levy on tech firms unless they strike news deals
items.summary: Australia approved a new News Bargaining Incentive that would require Meta, Google, TikTok, and LinkedIn to pay a levy if they do not reach commercial agreements with local publishers. Reuters and other outlets say the charge would equal 2.5% of advertising revenue in the affected market.

items.title: Charter completes $34.5 billion Cox acquisition
items.summary: Charter closed its long-awaited acquisition of Cox, uniting two major U.S. cable and broadband providers and completing its related Liberty transaction. The deal is one of the largest cable-industry consolidation moves in recent years.

items.title: Waymo opens Ojai vans to all riders in three cities
items.summary: Waymo expanded access to its autonomous van service, making the vehicles available to all riders in San Francisco, Phoenix, and Los Angeles. The rollout marks a broader public launch for the driverless vans.

items.title: GitHub suffered a major outage lasting nearly eight hours
items.summary: GitHub experienced an outage on August 17 that lasted 7 hours and 47 minutes. The incident is notable because it affected a core platform used widely by developers and software teams.

items.title: Apple Music will visibly label AI-generated songs
items.summary: Apple Music told industry partners that tracks tagged as "materially generated using AI" will be visibly labeled on the service. The move follows Apple's broader AI transparency labeling approach for music metadata.

items.title: OpenAI adds Apple Messages integration to ChatGPT on macOS
items.summary: OpenAI rolled out a Mac integration that lets ChatGPT read, search, and analyze Apple Messages conversations, and help prepare and send messages. The update deepens ChatGPT's connection to Apple’s ecosystem.

items.title: Ramp launches its internal AI model routing service
items.summary: Ramp introduced Router, an AI model routing service it says it has used internally for three years. The company is making the service free to use in the U.S. through the rest of 2026.

items.title: Alibaba profit falls as AI infrastructure spending rises
items.summary: Alibaba reported a 75% drop in quarterly profit while continuing to invest heavily in AI infrastructure. Even with the profit decline, revenue from its AI cloud and compute services grew 45% and total revenue rose 9%.

items.title: Unitree shares surge in Shanghai trading debut
items.summary: Chinese humanoid robot maker Unitree jumped as much as 629% in its Shanghai market debut and ended the session up 460%. The listing raised about $900 million, underscoring strong investor appetite for robotics.

items.title: Australia’s news bargaining policy widens pressure on Big Tech
items.summary: A second report on Australia’s policy says the levy would apply to Meta, Google, TikTok, and Microsoft’s LinkedIn if they fail to negotiate with publishers. The proposal has become one of the day’s biggest global tech-policy developments.
